The ACS will not publish a median value at this sample size, so that figure is suppressed and any site showing you one for Acampo is showing you something else. ZHVI is about 775,000 dollars, up 0.5 percent over the year.

So the buying questions are mostly postwar questions.

Pull the year built and the permit history for the parcel. On a tract house of this era, ask about the electrical panel and its capacity, the supply lines, the sewer lateral, the roof, and whether the foundation has ever been bolted.

An original kitchen and original aluminium windows are either the discount or the asset. The inspection report tells you which.

Get the tax bill for the address, not the listing estimate.

Then the part specific to this address. Confirm first that the address is unincorporated San Joaquin County territory, because it changes who issues your permits, who provides your services, who polices it and how your tax bill is built. Take it from the county, not from a listing. Then ask which school district serves the parcel. Ask whether the parcel is on sewer or on septic, and if septic, get the most recent inspection and the pumping record. Ask whether water comes from a district or a well, and if a well, get the yield and the water quality tests in writing. On valley agricultural ground, also ask what is farmed on the adjoining parcels and when it is sprayed. With 110 housing units and a suppressed median, there is almost no comparable sales record here. Ask for closed sales going back far enough to mean something and expect to reason from a handful. And establish what the housing actually is, because a 38.2 percent detached share in a place this small means much of it is not conventional detached housing.

Then drive your commute at the hour you would really drive it, and walk the block after dinner.

What the market is doing right now

Acampo sits at $774,585 in typical value as of 2026-09-30, having moved up 0.16 percent since last month and up 0.5 percent since last year.

Listing activity in Acampo for 2026-09. Active inventory is 16. 6 new listings came on, and 9 went pending. Median days on market is 45.

Median asking price is $925,000 at $485 per square foot.

The numbers

  • Typical home value: $774,585, up 0.16 percent month over month, up 0.5 percent over the year.
  • Monthly cost of owning it: $7,452, or $89,422 a year, HOA not included.
  • 30-year fixed: 7.4 percent as of 2026-10-15, against 6.27 percent a year earlier.
  • 2026 one-unit loan limit, San Joaquin County: $832,750. A minimum-down loan at the typical value sits inside it.
  • Effective property tax rate used: 1.23 percent (San Joaquin County effective rate).

What it costs to own here

Figure about $7,452 a month to own the typical home in Acampo, $89,422 a year. Loan, property tax, insurance, utilities and maintenance are in that figure. HOA dues are not, and they vary too much to average.

The 30-year fixed average is 7.4 percent as of 2026-10-15, against 6.27 percent in the same week last year. The conforming and FHA ceiling for a one-unit property in San Joaquin County is $832,750 in 2026.

The transfer tax line that costs real money

Transfer tax on the typical Acampo home, $774,585, comes to roughly $852 at a rate of 1.10 per thousand. Local practice splits it down the middle, roughly $426 each, though the contract decides.

What waiting costs

On the same trailing rate, two years of waiting adds up to roughly $9,652 in price and payment combined, and five years to $29,367.

The input is a single trailing year, projected. It is not a forecast, and the five year number is the one to distrust first.

item.title: Thornton, Thornton: the October 2026 read
item.description: What the Thornton, Thornton housing market is doing in October 2026. Typical value $451,446, up 0.06 percent month over month, plus the transfer tax bracket that costs real money and what waiting actually costs.
item.content:encoded:
Thornton is a small place, and the numbers below are the whole market.

Thornton is unincorporated San Joaquin County territory up on the Delta edge north of Stockton, and a quarter of its housing is pre war. Lodi to the east began as Mokelumne Station in 1869 and its renaming is given variously as 1873, 1874 and 1878.

Thornton has 291 housing units and 25.4 percent of them predate 1950, the highest pre war share of any place in this county. 71.5 percent are single family detached, owner occupancy runs 60.4 percent, and the ACS median value is 435,400 dollars. ZHVI is about 451,000 dollars, flat over the year.

So the first questions here are the old housing questions.

Pull the year built. On pre war stock, ask about foundation bolting, knob and tube wiring, galvanized supply lines, and the condition of the original windows and siding. Confirm the legal unit count with the city, not the listing, and get the permit history for the parcel.

Ask whether the building is nonconforming, because that limits what you can rebuild after a loss and it affects financing and insurance.

Get the tax bill for the address, not the listing estimate.

Then the part specific to this address. Confirm first that the address is unincorporated San Joaquin County territory, because it changes who issues your permits, who provides your services, who polices it and how your tax bill is built. Take it from the county, not from a listing. Then ask which school district serves the parcel. Get the flood zone determination for the parcel with a written insurance quote before your contingencies expire, and ask the inspector about drainage and about where water leaves the property in a wet month. This is Delta and valley floor ground and levee and flood mapping drive the insurance. Thornton sits in Delta country and the levee question is the central one, so ask the county and the reclamation district which levee protects the parcel and what its certification status is. Ask whether the parcel is on sewer or on septic, and if septic, get the most recent inspection and the pumping record. Ask whether water comes from a district or a well, and if a well, get the yield and the water quality tests in writing. On valley agricultural ground, also ask what is farmed on the adjoining parcels and when it is sprayed.

Then drive your commute at the hour you would really drive it, and walk the block after dinner.

What the market is doing right now

Typical home value in Thornton is $451,446 as of 2026-09-30, up 0.06 percent from the month before and down 0.0 percent over the year.

Listing activity in Thornton for 2026-09. Active inventory is 2. 0 new listings came on, and 1 went pending. Median days on market is 15.

Median asking price is $1,161,250 at $743 per square foot.

The numbers

  • Typical home value: $451,446, up 0.06 percent month over month, down 0.0 percent over the year.
  • Monthly cost of owning it: $4,692, or $56,307 a year, HOA not included.
  • 30-year fixed: 7.4 percent as of 2026-10-15, against 6.27 percent a year earlier.
  • 2026 one-unit loan limit, San Joaquin County: $832,750. A minimum-down loan at the typical value sits inside it.
  • Effective property tax rate used: 1.23 percent (San Joaquin County effective rate).

What it costs to own here

Figure about $4,692 a month to own the typical home in Thornton, $56,307 a year. Loan, property tax, insurance, utilities and maintenance are in that figure. HOA dues are not, and they vary too much to average.

As of 2026-10-15 the 30-year fixed averages 7.4 percent, up or down from 6.27 percent twelve months before. The 2026 one-unit loan limit in San Joaquin County is $832,750, and that figure is both the conforming ceiling and the FHA ceiling.

The transfer tax line that costs real money

Transfer tax on the typical Thornton home, $451,446, comes to roughly $497 at a rate of 1.10 per thousand. Expect it split, near enough $248 apiece, with the contract having the final say.

What waiting costs

On the same trailing rate, two years of waiting adds up to roughly -$23 in price and payment combined, and five years to -$69.

That rate is one observed year extrapolated forward, not a forecast, and compounding a single strong year out to five produces a large number by construction. Weight the two year figure more heavily.
